name: The Hole Under the Mountain
summary: Eleven masks on one table: one face, all smiling. The hole is new, and the oldest say the worst part is who it must have been. It is hungry, not hateful. One man came back: it asked politely.
body: Everything else in this book is the world working as it always has. This chapter is the exception. Read it, and then do not go east.

There is a cave under the eastern mountain. One mouth, not hidden; every person in Nangijala can tell you roughly where it is. Nobody ever needed a legend to find it. The whole difficulty runs the other way.

Near it, things forget faster. That was measured carefully, by people who wanted it to be wrong: ground held for centuries — in the rota, with a fire on it — went soft in a season, and then the season became a month. A keeper on the eastern circuit lost the name of her own fire walking toward the mouth and had it back within the hour of walking away, and she was not a woman anyone had known to lose anything. [[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]], who maps the Drift, still walks the eastern line every year. He has stopped telling anybody what he measures.

Out in the wild a beast is [[lore/the_quiet|a shape that outlasted whoever was in it]], running on habit, empty, wanting almost nothing from you. The creatures near the mouth are not that. They were not left empty — they were emptied, all at once, and something else is wearing the outside. The word is Hollowed. The trade will not take money to touch them.

Break one and a mask comes down out of it and lands in the dirt, still smiling — the little dark [[monsters/masked_shadow_creature|Grinmask]] is the one most often seen to drop one. A mask does not thin. It lies in the grass being exactly a face after everything else has stopped being anywhere at all. For years the comfortable explanation was that a face is simply the last part of a person to let go of — the piece the emptying could not take. Then [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] borrowed every mask anyone had kept — eleven, from eleven creatures broken years and miles apart — and laid them out in a row on one table.

Not eleven faces that happen to be alike. One face, eleven times, the way eleven drawings by eleven hands of one person are one face — never quite agreeing, unmistakably the same attempt. No straps, no eye-holes, no wear. Nothing ever wore these. They were made, one after another, by something that keeps missing what it reaches for by a width nobody can name. Except the smile. The smile is identical on all eleven. Nobody says the comfortable thing any more.

There has been one organised attempt on the cave. One, ever. The best the fires had went in on a summer morning, and in the evening [[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] came back out alone, unhollowed, unmarked. Everyone has asked him what is inside — the kind, the cruel, the drunk, [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] with her book open — and all of them got the same three words: it asked politely. He buys rounds he cannot afford for people who are not there to drink them. The others never re-formed at any fire anybody keeps, and nobody who walks the east road at dusk looks closely at the shapes they pass, in case of knowing a walk.

Two things are checkable, and they are the worst facts in this book. The first: the hole is new. Not new the way a season is new — new the way a wound is. The [[lore/the_age_of_fires|Age of Fires]] had no hole under the eastern mountain. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] was already old when the east road was just a road, and for an evening of company he will give you what that was like: carts, he says, and dust, and somebody always singing badly over the hill. He once slept on the open ground above where the mouth is now. Then he stops trading.

The second: count what it takes. Not ground, not meat, not blood — names. Faces, voices, the thing you were about to say. It wants what people are made of, the way a person wants: one thing, terribly, without being able to stop. Habit does not want like that; weather does not want at all. The oldest finished that thought years ago and have not said it since: the hole was almost certainly somebody. And the worst part, they say, is not what it is now. The worst part is who it must have been then.

[[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] once got one of them to go further, and printed the exchange in [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]] without comment. Whoever it was had a grip, the old man said. Somebody who could hold on after everyone else had let go. And if you want to be kept awake, girl: think of who we all trusted with our worst hour. Who came to you in the grass before you could stand, and sat down a little way off, and spoke gently, and asked. Then he told her to bank the fire, and that was the interview.

The last fact is the one the tellers insist on. Nothing about it is angry. In the whole record there is no malice — no vengeance, no spite, nothing done for the sake of the doing. It has never hated anyone. It is hungry. That is all it is, and hunger is what waiting turns into when it stops being able to end.
Nobody knows what it was waiting for. Do not go east.
